title: Existence of a counit-normalized trace on one dualizing quotient system
statement:
theorem integralDualizingSystemTraceData_exists
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S)
    (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (eQ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≅
        integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n)
    (hQ : ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≫
          (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (eQ n).hom =
        (eQ m).hom ≫
          (Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (normalizedDVRRes l E X h)).homEquiv _ _
            (integralDualizingFiniteComparison l E D X hl h)) :
    Nonempty (IntegralDualizingSystemTraceData D l E X S G Q eQ)

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: Use the scalar-restriction descriptions of open extension and proper image to identify the support functor with the native quotient-system one. The tensor-unit universal property gives its finite unit comparisons. Represent Q on a simultaneous quotient-system resolution.

At every finite level apply eQ, the fixed etale origin, and the etale exceptional counit. The finite exceptional coefficient counit square and hQ make these maps compatible with every quotient; rectify the counit word on the simultaneous resolution and descend it. No test input is involved.
Exact evaluation of this same resolution gives the displayed trace_evaluation equation, including its fixed support and site comparison factors.
